where: PV family: sim/pv_control.py load_params -> ctrl_init/ctrl_outer -> DA/DB and ilim; cell_spec ratings.I_max_A_low_voltage_port
finding: Port-current rating reused as the inductor-current ceiling. 45 A is loaded from a low-voltage-port rating and then clamps mean phase-inductor current. With DA=DB=0.94333 at 550/550 V, three phases transfer at most 70.042 kW before loss. Even without this duty loss, 75 kW/550 V=136.36 A exceeds 135 A.
evidence: CODE-VERIFIED; INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED. Sources S03 S04 S07 S08
recommendation: Separate phase mean/RMS/peak limits from port-current limits; publish a direction- and mode-dependent delivered-power envelope. Do not raise the phase limit without rechecking hardware and trips.
closure: The 45 A term was the cell's low-voltage-port rating applied to the inductor current in every mode; in the near-unity band (both legs switching, D_max 0.94333 set by the 1.771 us minimum pulse = 0.6 us on-time + 2 x 586 ns dead-time stretch, kept per D-050) the ports carried 127 A = 70.0 kW at 550/550 V. Fixed in sim/pv_control.py (D-065): the inductor limit is the inductor's own rms design rating from cell_spec (47.70 A) in that band and 45 A in buck/boost; the port limits (PV 135/180 A, battery 135/145 A) stay separate and duty-converted. At the band limit every hardware value stays inside its design point (peak 52.3 A vs 62.3 A, device 46.3 A rms = design, inductor copper loss 50.6 W vs 83.8 W worst, hottest junction 109.5 C). Envelope published (envelope.csv, control_spec.json, report section 12.3): 550/550 V 73.3 kW; PV-P75 rated from 562 V at equal port voltages both ways at 35/45 C. 75 kW at exactly 550 V needs 136.4 A: the requirement set (PV-04/07 vs PV-05/08) is inconsistent by 1 % at that corner, published as such. Calculated, not measured.

where: PV family: PV control model -> CTRL-C2000/LA 150-P assumptions versus PV-CTL/F280039C/STK-HO/A 75 and actual port banks
finding: Current control evidence still uses the earlier hardware model. The reported control stability and accuracy chain is not the same plant, sensor chain, controller timing or capacitance as the cost-first build. P75 B-port capacitance is 334.8 uF including local films, rather than the old symmetric 274.4 uF example.
evidence: CODE-VERIFIED; REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY. Sources S06 S07 S08 S09 S10 S11
recommendation: Rebuild closed-loop models from a versioned current-board interface manifest, including actual AFE poles/noise, ADC scheduling, quantization, trips and source/load dynamics.
closure: The loop evidence modelled the CTRL-C2000 / LA 150-P chain and a 274.4 uF example. Re-based on the drawn boards (D-065): port banks 289.8 / 334.8 uF (four-phase 386.4), STK-HO/A 75 + PV-CTL AFE (0.81 us, 0.0722 A/LSB, 2.3 A pp noise), 17 conversions per 31.25 us, lean-shunt 11.3 kHz, V/1203 dividers 6.8 kHz, trips from cell_spec. Result: current loop 2282-2750 Hz, PM >= 57.6 deg, GM >= 11.6 dB; two samples of delay 42.6-46.0 deg (one-sample computation delay stays a firmware requirement); the reviewer's reduced-model margins (56.7-58.6 / 40.8-44.9 deg) reproduced within 1-2 deg; CPL corner 44.3 deg (3 ph) / 45.0 deg (4 ph); load rejection 1023.8 V; port-B bank needed 243 uF (drawn 334.8 uF, the 7th capacitor kept as a cost lever). The earlier-platform CTRL-C2000 now checks against a frozen snapshot of the spec it was designed to (gen/data/control_spec_platform1.json).

where: PCS-P125: gen/pcs_power.py leg_nets/sheet_leg/sheet_dclink -> DC+/DC- -> C201-C210 plus 27 local C301..C513; BOM items 1/2 -> K1802 precharge
finding: Local film capacitance omitted from precharge/discharge calculations. 350 uF is the split bulk bank only. The 27 x 2.2 uF local films add 59.4 uF across the same rails. Known total is 409.4 uF: 950 V precharge energy 184.74 J, not 157.94 J; 220-ohm time constant 90.07 ms, not 77 ms. A reduced passive RC tolerance case takes 16.17 min to 60 V and remains at 73.69 V at 15 min.
evidence: CODE-VERIFIED; BOM-VERIFIED; INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED; ACTUALLY SIMULATED. Sources S12 S14 S15
recommendation: Use the complete connected capacitor inventory for precharge, bleeders, pulse-energy qualification, timing and service label. Include AC-filter and auxiliary storage in the final discharge network.
closure: Accounting error: precharge, bleeder and the 15 min label used the 350 uF split bank only. Fixed at the root (sim/pcs_design.py, gen/port.py): DC-link total 409.4 uF (450.3 uF at +10 %) including the 27 x 2.2 uF leg films; precharge at 950 V 184.7 J / 90 ms, worst case from the 1050 V trip 248 J at 104 ms, shorted bank 762 J in 0.14 s; the precharge-resistor rating (shared RPRE_AL) raised from 180 J / 600 J to 280 J at 105 ms / 900 J in 0.15 s (still covers the PV ports: 241-278 J / 774-864 J); bleeder 4 x 110 k -> 4 x 93.1 k per half: worst case to 60 V 14.7 min (was 17.0 min with the real network; 13.3 min nominal) including C_f + C_d (60 uF per phase) and the 6.6 uF aux bulk, so the 'wait 15 min' label stays; standby loss at 950 V +0.19 W (1.21 W). C_f and C_d discharge through their 6 M dividers and, via the body diodes, the bus bleeders - never above the bus, no separate bleeder. PCS-PWR rebuilt and passes. Thin margin (14.7 vs 15 min) stated.

where: PCS-P125: 02_dclink -> VA=V(M)-V(DC-), VB=V(DC+)-V(DC-); C201-C205 upper, C206-C210 lower
finding: Upper DC-link half is not directly covered by the shown half-voltage trip. Total-bus and lower-half comparators do not by themselves bound V(DC+)-V(M). A high upper-half voltage with low midpoint can evade the lower-half threshold. Equal bleeders correct static imbalance slowly; they do not prove transient balance.
evidence: CODE-VERIFIED; INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED. Sources S12 S13 S14
recommendation: Explicitly calculate upper=VB-VA after calibrated scaling and add a sufficiently fast, justified protection path. Model tolerance, leakage, startup, common-mode injection and open-divider faults.
closure: Mechanisms that can over-voltage the upper half with VB < 1050 V and VA < 560 V (pcs_design.py 1775): +/-10 % capacitance split at precharge 578 V (0.96 x U_N at 70 C, static, bled out in minutes); one lower-half capacitor shorted 950 V (1.58 x U_N) for the ~20 ms until the DC contactor opens; an open upper bleeder string drifts toward 927 V reaching the firmware limit after 1.3 min; C_f-star current (150 Hz + switching) 534 V ripple, no drift; zero-sequence step 576 V transient. The only fast case ends with the contactor's own ~10 ms release, far longer than the firmware's <= 72.5 us latency, so no comparator is added (SRC-7, D-050). Firmware rule in pcs_spec / PCS-CTL check: trip at VB - VA >= 540 V, shorted-half detection, slow imbalance limit |VA - VB/2| > 0.07 VB for 1 s; latency confirmed on the control board's own sampling plan (VA/VB every 7.8 us). Residual second-failure risk (a shorted capacitor stresses the other half beyond rating for ~20 ms) stated.

where: PCS-P125: PCS limits -> L1/L2 -> modulation and grid contactor permissive
finding: DC, AC, P, Q and overload limits cannot be rectangular. 460 V line-line requires at least 650.54 V DC under ideal SVPWM, before filter and control headroom. Thus 590/600 V DC cannot support the complete +15% grid range. 125 kW at 400 V needs 180.42 A; 150 kVA needs 216.51 A, near the 216 A two-minute tier rather than 198 A continuous.
evidence: INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED; CODE-VERIFIED. Sources S13 S16 S17
recommendation: Publish one combined P-Q-Vdc-Vac-frequency-temperature map and enforce it in startup, rectification, inversion, reactive power and grid-forming limits.
closure: Envelope published (pcs_design.py 2219-2259, pcs_spec.json, report): minimum DC voltage with a 5 % loop headroom and the 510 ns dead-time compensation (both assumed): 400 V grid 624 V to connect, 605-643 V for rated current depending on power factor; 460 V grid 698-737 V (741 V at 60 Hz); with 590-600 V DC only grids up to about 360 V can be served. 125 kW at 400 V = 180.4 A; 150 kVA = 216.5 A = the 2-minute tier, not the 198 A continuous one. Uncontrolled rectification (460 V grid on a 590 V battery, gates off) 846 A peak / 730 A DC stiff, 113 / 98 A at SCR 5 - hence the firmware rows: modulation-index limiter, AC-contactor closing permissive (V_dc above the grid peak plus margin), the under-voltage reaction (which contactor opens, release time, current meanwhile), overload tiers in kVA per grid voltage. OPEN requirement decision: AC-02's 'full load from 600 V at 400 V +/-15 %' is not reachable with these margins (owner's call; REQUIREMENTS.md not edited).

where: PCS-P125: Q301-Q306 / Q307-Q312, repeated on B/C; per-gate resistors and Kelvin sources; hot-device thermal model
finding: Ten-percent current-sharing allowance is not established for six parallel devices. An illustrative bank with one 40 mOhm and five 52 mOhm devices has the low-resistance device at 1.238 times the equal-share current. A same-lot or Vth-bin rule alone does not establish a 1.10 conduction-current bound; hot minimum/maximum distributions remain unbounded.
evidence: DATASHEET-CONFIRMED; INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED; LAYOUT-DEPENDENT. Sources S12 S15 S17 D01
recommendation: Define incoming Rds/threshold/sharing acceptance at relevant temperatures and validate dynamic sharing with the actual gate/Kelvin/busbar geometry. Recalculate the hottest device, not only average bank loss.
closure: The 1.30 share factor of D-057 bounded only the 60 C / 100 % rating; with the datasheet-only population (one 40 mOhm device among five at 52 mOhm, positive temperature coefficient applied) the hottest device carries 1.22 x the mean and the 45 C 200 ms tier would reach 186 C (rating 175 C). Fix: an acceptance rule on the SG2M040170HJ BOM line (pcs_design.py 1155-1268): R_DS(on) of the six devices of a switch matched within +/-5 % at V_GS 18 V, 38 A pulsed, 25 C; V_GS(th) within +/-0.25 V; one lot per switch -> hottest device <= 1.08 x mean, every 45 C tier holds; at 60 C firmware derates the 200 ms tier to 246 A. Binning feasibility and cost with Sichain unconfirmed (open).

where: PCS-P125: NSI6651 channels -> DESAT diode string -> six-device bank; overload current limit
finding: DESAT low threshold overlaps hot overload on-state voltage. At the manufacturer typical 175 C Rds of 88 mOhm, 66 A/device produces about 5.81 V, above the reported 5.43 V minimum DESAT threshold. This does not prove a trip at a lower actual junction temperature, but the hot-overload corner is not coordinated.
evidence: DATASHEET-CONFIRMED; INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED; REQUIRES HARDWARE TEST. Sources S14 S21 D01
recommendation: Recompute normal-current and DESAT threshold distributions with measured/guaranteed device temperature and dynamic Vds. Re-coordinate short-circuit protection before changing thresholds or blanking.
closure: DESAT string reduced from 3 to 2 x US1MH per channel (gen/gdrv.py PCS preset; six fewer diodes per board): trip band 5.43-8.27 V -> 6.41-9.17 V with the drawn Taiwan Semi US1MH forward curve (0.30-1.01 V per diode). Margin at the 200 ms overload peak (66.2 A per device): 1.08 at the predicted 161 C junction (45 C inlet), 1.00 at the 175 C rating, 1.57 at -30 C. Short circuit: a hard short trips in 1.47 us (within the assumed 2 us withstand), a fault under load is detected at <= 138 A per device (I_DM 188 A), booster turn-off overshoot 1212 V vs 1445 V. Design check no longer prints OPEN (1). Open: V_F at 0.5 mA extrapolated from typical curves - measure; the 175 C margin is 1.00.

where: PV / PCS / proposed DAB: Shared gate presets -> assumed SCWT, assumed short-circuit current, hot Vth scaling and FIT arguments
finding: Short-circuit, hot threshold and reliability assumptions are not device guarantees. Current SG2M040170HJ data support 1700 V, 188 A pulsed rating and 175 C maximum junction, but do not supply the short-circuit withstand, hot Vth minimum, selected-device cosmic-ray FIT or qualification evidence used to close those reliability arguments. Pulsed ID is not short-circuit survival.
evidence: DATASHEET-CONFIRMED; CODE-VERIFIED; REQUIRES HARDWARE TEST. Sources S05 S20 S21 D01
recommendation: Obtain device-specific evidence and production traceability, or qualify a controlled substitute. Bound SC current/energy and hot false-turn-on independently; do not scale another manufacturer into a safety guarantee.
closure: Supplier-evidence gate, already registered as risks A2 / C2 / C6: no Chinese 1700 V or 1200 V SiC maker publishes a short-circuit withstand, a hot V_GS(th) minimum, a cosmic-ray FIT curve or a qualification report; nothing in schematic scope can close it. Kept as a release block; the fallback for PV-P75 is the qualified Microchip MSC035SMA170B4 assembly variant (D-043), none priced for the 36-device PCS. The LCSC sourcing pass of 2026-10-05 (sim/data/lcsc_semis.md) records which makers state AEC-Q101 on the datasheet.

where: DAB-D60: gen/dab60.py frozen B0 -> CBB011M12GM4T/UCC21710 versus dab_spec IV3Q12013T4Z/NSI6651 proposal
finding: New DAB study is not the frozen DAB60 implementation. The existing frozen source uses the older module/driver architecture. The current study uses different discrete devices, drive timing, bias and magnetics. Excluding the frozen board from regeneration does not make the proposal its validated implementation.
evidence: CODE-VERIFIED; REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY. Sources S02 S19 S20
recommendation: Create a separate revision/assembly identity for the new DAB, redraw it, export and bind its BOM/model/firmware interfaces. Keep old results segregated.
closure: The committed dab_spec.json held the D2W discrete study (IV3Q12013T4Z / SG2M014120LJ, NSI6651) under the key gen/dab60.py asserts as CBB011M12GM4T, with old module-round text. Fixed: an 'assembly' block in dab_spec.json and the report header state that DAB60 rev B0 (2 x CBB011M12GM4T, UCC21710, +15/-4 V) is the drawn board and the D2W study has no schematic; which result belongs to which is listed (study: efficiency/derating maps, stresses, decks, DESAT and trip chains; control study: common plant n 0.9167 / 6.50 uH / 150 uH, study devices' R_loop and OC trip, not acceptance evidence for rev B); stale module-round statements removed. where: Proposed DAB-D60: dab_spec DESAT blanking/turn-off -> assumed SC withstand
finding: Calculated fault response exceeds even the assumed withstand. The proposal gives roughly 1.765 us total response against a 1.12 us assumed withstand. The ratio is about 1.58. Neither number is a device-specific qualification, but they do not close even the internal budget.
evidence: REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY; INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED. Sources S20
recommendation: Replace the borrowed survival estimate and rework the complete fault timing/energy chain, including blanking, detection, driver behavior, external booster, current decay and overshoot.
closure: Chain corrected (dab_design.py DR-05): the 2026-10-04 chain added the NSI6651's 265 ns deglitch on top of the 300 ns DESAT-to-output delay although the datasheet times both from the same threshold crossing (NSI66x1A Fig. 8.10 p23), and its '0.97x' was withstand/chain. Honest endpoint: in a short V_DS stays at the bus so no Miller plateau holds the current - it falls with the gate voltage from the moment the gate starts falling; the reviewer's 1.58 (full current to the plateau) is refuted on that physics, as is 0.97. Corrected chain (SG2M014120LJ, NSI6651 industrial worst case): blanking 592 ns, gate falling 892 ns (0.80x), plateau 1297 ns (1.16x), V_th 1552 ns (1.39x), energy-equivalent full-current time 1112 ns = 0.99x the assumed 1.12 us hot withstand; fault energy 1.09 J per device vs 1.10 J assumed. Release block unchanged: maker-confirmed t_SC >= 2.22 us at 1000 V / 150 C (about 4.0 us at 800 V / 25 C) and E_SC >= 2.18 J, or a short-circuit test, or a device with a published withstand. No lever inside the NSI6651 reaches the 0.5 the 2x rule needs (best: booster + 10 k pull-up 0.61). Same root cause fixed in DR-03 (fault peak 632 A, per-maker I_DM, series-inductor saturation requirement 700 A). The shared gdrv.py chain of the PV/PCS presets carried the same double count (corrected, conservative by 265 ns).

where: Proposed DAB-D60: dab_spec commutation results -> 1200 V proposed devices, hard-turn-on prohibition and timing windows
finding: Reported commutation peaks exceed the proposed 1200 V rating. The study contains peaks around 1232 V and hard-turn-on cases around 1398-1437 V. These were not rerun here. A claimed model overprediction factor taken from a different device is not a valid clearance of a rating exceedance.
evidence: REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY; REQUIRES HARDWARE TEST; LAYOUT-DEPENDENT. Sources S20
recommendation: Calibrate the actual device model and parasitic network, then establish an operating/dead-time map which excludes unsafe commutations or change the design. Retain the raw failing cases.
closure: Deck results reproduced (1236 V at 950/900 V 60 kW; hard turn-on 1398/1437 V); at 950 V the deck overshoot does not fall with power (278-318 V for any 58-141 A turn-off), so no deck power at 950/900 V reaches 1200 V. The admitted map now follows the deck envelope with the limit 1200 V = V_DSS (no maker publishes a repetitive rating; the GM4 1.47x factor is information only): turn-off current limit 54 A at 950 V, 58 A at 900 V; 950 V row 12.5 kW at 950/900 V, 10 kW at 950/850 V; 900 V row 10/15/25 kW at V2 800/850/900 V; full-power window 11 of 20 points (was 16; lost 700/900, 800/900, 900/800, 900/850, 900/900 V); hard turn-on excluded by the LUT rule V_bus + V_res <= 1200 V re-checked by firmware at start (FW-DAB-2). Calibrated efficiency claim 99.09 % peak, 98.80 % at 800/800 V 60 kW, minimum 97.94 %. Only a double-pulse test on the real layout can restore the 900-950 V rows.

where: Proposed DAB-D60: 11:12 transformer, 6.5 uH, 100 kHz -> SPS periodic waveform and operating LUT
finding: Zero transferred power can still produce excessive SPS circulating current. At 950/400 V and zero SPS phase shift, calculated primary series current is 129.53 A RMS and 224.36 A peak if both bridges keep switching. Necessary secondary ZVS polarity is wrong. The 590/400 V SPS ceiling is 41.60 kW, and the 100 A second-port limit reduces ideal usable power to 40 kW.
evidence: INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED. Sources S20
recommendation: Validate TPS/EPS/DPS or bridge-off/burst policies where they meaningfully reduce circulation. Include transition trajectories, power reversal, startup, magnetizing current and flux balance.
closure: Reviewer's numbers confirmed (SPS, zero shift, 950/400 V: 129.53 A rms / 224.36 A peak; 590/400 V SPS ceiling 41.60 kW; 100 A port-2 limit 40 kW; admitted map 37.5 kW at 590/400 V). There was no idle rule: the committed LUT at 950/400 V, 2.5 kW circulated 72.9 A rms. Policy FW-DAB-1..7 in sim/dab_control.py / dab_spec: switch only on admitted LUT entries (inner shifts up to 150 deg: 950/400 V 2.5 kW now 19.0 A rms / 53.5 A peak); gates off below 1.5 kW, on again at 2.5 kW (or the lowest admitted row); single phase shift only where |V1 - n V2| <= 130 V; light-load bound <= 44 A rms / 93 A peak up to 10 kW everywhere; admitted set covers V1/(n V2) 0.73-2.59. Time domain: soft start from idle 119 A peak / 3.3 A DC offset; reversal through zero 4 idle periods, 115 A peak. Not simulated: start from idle on a large-mismatch TPS entry.

where: PV-P100 / PV-P110: PV-PWR-4 -> battery port, fan/cooling and 4-phase controller limits
finding: Four phases do not remove the 145 A battery-port and thermal restrictions. 145 A at Port B requires at least 689.66 V for 100 kW and 758.62 V for 110 kW, before loss. At 690 V input only 100.05 kW is available, so reverse 100 kW delivered leaves essentially no loss allowance. The documented four-phase full-power inlet restriction is 35 C, not automatically the P75 45 C requirement.
evidence: REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY; INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED. Sources S01 S05 S10
recommendation: Publish separate P100 and P110 delivered-power/direction/temperature envelopes and validate port, inductor, capacitor and fan limits jointly.
closure: The four-phase scenario took a 180 A battery port and its derating table from P75-era constants. Now (D-065) it takes the 145 A battery port and the full-power-to-35 C derating from the four-phase entries of module_spec, and PV-P100 / PV-P110 are published as separate envelopes (envelope.csv): P100 rated from 690 V A->B and 697 V B->A at 35 C; P110 delivers 108.8 kW A->B at any voltage because the 27.5 kW per-phase limit is held at the source side (110 kW is an input-side rating), B->A 110 kW from 765 V at 35 C only; at 60 C no product reaches its rating (table in the report). Any phase count other than 1, 3 or 4 stops the run. The reviewer's 689.66 / 758.62 V (145 A before loss) are reproduced.

where: PV and PCS: AUX75 live winding -> +5V/+3V3, bias supplies and economized contactor coils
finding: Auxiliary rail budgets have little reserve and PCS coil pickup is not closed. P75 live rail is budgeted at 19.8/20.0 W; PV4 at 23.7/24.0 W; PCS about 23.1/24.0 W with AC coil hold power still an RFQ assumption. Total converter wattage does not establish per-winding dynamic capability. Added gate capacitance, cold coils, retries and cross-regulation must be included.
evidence: REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY; INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED; REQUIRES HARDWARE TEST. Sources S09 S10 S14
recommendation: Bind exact coil pickup/hold envelopes and all gate loads; perform rail-wise low/high-line, cold/hot, startup and simultaneous-transient analysis. Sequence contactors where appropriate; increase capacity if the bounded load needs it.
closure: PV: the live-24 V budgets (19.8/20.0 W, 23.7/24.0 W) are stacks of datasheet maxima with the pull-in cases (a)/(b) bounded against the 32 W live peak and a 25 ms hold-up (PV-PWR check). PCS: step budget added (PCS-PWR check): DC contactor pull-in 21.7 W, each AC contactor relay-test pull-in 31.4 W, synchronised close with PWM running 38.9 W (6.9 W over the 32 W peak with an ASSUMED 20 W / 100 ms coil pull-in), running 22.9 W (5 % reserve), hold-up 26 ms. Firmware rules added: never two coils at once; AC contactor 2 only after 1 has settled; retries >= 10 s apart, 3 per start, then lockout; immediate lockout on a welded contact. Remedy named, not drawn: shift the aux transformer's live/SELV split to >= 29 W continuous / >= 43 W peak (no BOM cost) once the AC coil is selected, or specify the coil at <= 13.1 W pull-in - decided when the RFQ coil data exist (risk F10).

where: DC ports / PCS: PCS F1603/F1604 HCHVF1000-400A-38R -> K1801 HFE82V-300C -> source/busbar fault loop
finding: Fuse I-squared-t comparison does not establish contactor survival. Hongfa warns about high-current contact bounce and welding; its short-current limits are not a single constant I-squared-t rule. Comparing the report's 290 kA2s and 384 kA2s alone does not bound peak let-through, minimum interruption current, polarity, L/R or arc voltage.
evidence: DATASHEET-CONFIRMED; CODE-VERIFIED; REQUIRES HARDWARE TEST. Sources S14 S15 D02
recommendation: Use the selected fuse cut-off/clearing curves and actual prospective source fault model, including both ports and external protection. Check harness, shunt, capacitor and contactor withstand together.
closure: Coordination computed (sim/port_design.py 2084-2203, read by the PCS-PWR check; OPEN (4) replaced): the 387-413 A over-current window opens the contactor, which can make 2.3 openings at 1033 A; 0.97-2.01 kA: nothing clears quickly - installation requirement that the battery side clears it within 2.5 s (as risk B6 for the PV port); 2.0-7.4 kA: the 400 A fuses protect the contactor; above 7.5 kA prospective the contactor's short-circuit capacity (8 kA for 6 ms, 10 kA for 1.5 ms) is exceeded - installation requirement to limit the prospective current or interrupt upstream. The old 290 vs 384 kA2s test used the 8 kA point only. Open: the fuse curve does not match its tabulated I2t (curve read conservatively, risk A5).

where: PV cost-first Port A: PV Port A contactor/MOV path without the same B-port fuse/precharge hardware
finding: A current-limited PV port is not automatically a generic stiff DC source port. The power stage can reverse power, but a PV-optimized unfused/unprecharged A-side interface does not by itself qualify a stiff battery/DC source, uncontrolled backfeed or upstream capacitor connection.
evidence: CODE-VERIFIED; REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY. Sources S01 S06 S09
recommendation: Declare admissible source type, external fusing, connection sequence, source capacitance and reverse-power permission. Use a protected port derivative when the application exceeds that contract.
closure: No interface declaration existed. gen/pv_power.py now prints a PORT A DECLARATION block (calculated, estimates labelled; no hardware change): port A admits a current-limited PV array only - I_sc at the terminals <= 168.8 A (1.25 x 135 A; K_A breaks 300 A at 1000 V both polarities), V_oc <= 1000 V (OV band 1039-1110 V), string fuses and a load-break isolator in the combiner, array/cable capacitance <= 1.1 uF behind >= 11 uH; K_A closes only with the latch clear, VAX above the polarity enable, the IMD in range and, with port B live, after the converter pre-charged the 290 uF A bank to within 20 V (making current = the array's I_sc). Not admitted: closing onto the empty bank at V_oc (about 499 A making current, ESTIMATE, against a published making rating of 140 A at 20 V only - Hongfa to confirm, risk R-04 stays open); reverse power B->A into an array (no series diode, fuse or precharge: firmware holds port A current >= 0); a stiff DC source (about 7.4 kA peak, weld likely) - that needs the PV-PORT-180 / lean port with fuse and precharge. Carried into the guide.

where: PV family: Delta AFB1224SHE-F00 / derivative fan choice -> inlet-temperature derating
finding: The selected fan does not establish the -30 C operating claim. The AFB fan operating range is -10 to +60 C. Its -40 C storage limit is not an operating qualification. The repository proposes fans off below -10 C, but the permissible passive-cooled power is not modeled.
evidence: DATASHEET-CONFIRMED; REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY; MECHANICAL-DEPENDENT. Sources S03 S05 D04
recommendation: Qualify a low-temperature fan/grease option, or declare startup lockout and a tested passive-power restriction. Separately bound altitude, dirty filters, fan failure and recirculation.
closure: The fan's -10 C limit was known (risk A4, D-045) but the passive-cooled power was not modelled. sim/pv_module.py now carries a passive model (natural-convection R_sa of the heatsink and inductors, a 2.4 W/K enclosure, 24 kJ/K structure; limits heatsink 75 C, inductor 130 C, T_j 125 C; ESTIMATES +/-50 %), exported as the cold-start restriction in module_spec.json and as a firmware-table row on PV-CTL: PV-P75 19.2 / 17.5 / 15.5 kW at -30 / -20 / -10 C inlet (pessimistic 6.8 / 0 / 0 kW), PV-P100/110 19.9 / 14.9 / 5.0 kW; the inlet warms from -30 to -10 C in about 45-48 min; at 611/611 V there is no passive power (the fans start on the heatsink override). Firmware rule: below -10 C inlet the fans stay off and power is limited to the table value; fans enabled once the inlet NTC reads above -10 C, at once at heatsink NTC >= 80 C or inductor NTC >= 135 C. Fan alternatives priced, not adopted: Sanyo 9GT1224P1S001 (-30 C) +225-300 USD per module and over the SELV allocation; ebm-papst 4414/2HHP (-20 C only) +63-198 USD. PV-20's -30 C holds at reduced power only; unvalidated estimates.

where: PV family: Jianghai bank/local capacitors -> sim/spice/pv_dpt_leg_dec.cir -> Vds/Miller/capacitor stress
finding: Updated capacitor ESL has not been incorporated into the reported commutation result. The current design check itself lists changed bank/local ESL versus the older KEMET deck and calls for a rerun. The earlier 1401 V result and false-turn-on margin are therefore not a validation of the changed assembly.
evidence: REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY; LAYOUT-DEPENDENT; REQUIRES HARDWARE TEST. Sources S09 S10
recommendation: Update the physical commutation model using actual capacitor impedance versus frequency and wiring allocation; calibrate against the prototype.
closure: The PV-PWR check itself flagged the stale ESL (OPEN R-08). The leg commutation deck now carries the drawn Jianghai FCSA3DS parts (bank FCSA3DS456 45 uF, 3 x FCSA3DS225 per leg, ESL/ESR from their datasheet) and gen/pv_power.py asserts the deck parts equal the drawn parts and the two decks agree within 1 V; ngspice results (calculated): V_DS peak 1274.8 / 1281.0 V at 1000 V and 62.3 / 72.5 A, 1367.0 / 1374.4 V at 1100 V (gates-off corner) against the 1445 V limit (71 V margin; the earlier KEMET-based 1373.8 V moved by +0.6 V); the held-off device's gate stays at +1.21..+1.40 V at the die against V_GS(th)min 1.94 V at 175 C (0.54 V margin, design margin 0.5 V); FCSA3DS225 current 34-38 A peak (61.5 A with the Q_rr surrogate) against 176 A, 3.1-3.6 A rms against 3.9 A at 85 C. The bolted-port-short clamp study was also re-run on the drawn bank (ESR 2.0 vs 1.55 mOhm, ESL 17.5 vs 9.5 nH): clamp duty unchanged within +0.5 %; the bank-internal reversal worsens to -104 V (3 cells) / -92 V (4 cells) and neither capacitor datasheet gives a reversal allowance (open). The headline 1401 V is now labelled as the lumped 20 nH deck without a capacitor model. No hardware change.

where: PV-CTL / inherited analog design: TLV9024 local OC window -> ILn_P and sensor Uref -> fault latch
finding: Comparator common-mode contribution is omitted from printed trip bands. The report explicitly excludes the offset change allowed by comparator CMRR from its PASS band. Its own 60/50 dB examples imply about 2.45/7.75 mV at 2.45 V common mode, roughly 0.31/0.97 A at the attenuated current node. This can consume the reported 0.4 A lower-bound clearance.
evidence: REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY; INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED. Sources S11
recommendation: Use the applicable guaranteed CMRR/offset/timing bounds at actual rail, common mode, temperature and overdrive in every window. Recompute normal-current clearance and fault peak simultaneously.
closure: The common-mode term was missing from every TLV9024 band. gen/pv_ctrl.py now adds |V_cm| / 10^(CMRR/20) with the guaranteed 50 dB (the lower of the 60 dB at 5 V and 50 dB at 1.8 V figures; 3.3 V is unspecified) and the datasheet propagation delay at the actual overdrive (283 ns typ at 16 mV, x2 ASSUMED) instead of 1.0 us ASSUMED: IL window 68.9-79.9 A / 1.95 us -> 67.9-80.5 A / 1.52 us (CM error 0.98 A (+) / 0.51 A (-)); gates off 1.52 us against 6.92 us, peak 91.1 A against 129 A. The project's 1.10 x normal-peak floor (68.5 A) is NOT met by 0.58 A and the top is 0.58 A over the 79.9 A cap: the fixed error terms (5.84 A) exceed the corridor half-width (5.69 A), so no E96 ladder value restores it; 10 ppm/K resistors alone give 68.1 A, 60 dB alone 68.6 A, both 68.8-79.8 A (fits). Decision: the window stays as drawn with a 1.09 margin, the shortfall printed as an [OPEN] item (its consequence is a nuisance trip at the worst ripple corner with every tolerance stacked, not a hazard); closing path: measure the TLV9024 CMRR at 3.3 V on samples (>= 60 dB) and fit 10 ppm/K ladder resistors (0.74 USD, D-058). OV band 1058-1110 -> 1039-1110 V: its bottom sat 10.9 V below the fixed 1050 V firmware controlled-stop limit, so the controlled stop is now derived from the drawn band (5 V below its bottom: 1034 V, sim/pv_design.py / control_spec). OT and open-probe bands move by < 0.2 K / 10 mV. The PCS-CTL variant inherits the term (OV ladder re-centred to 978-1048 V, window 426-486 A).

where: PCS-P125: RFQ IL1-3/IL1R-3R -> fixed 4 mV/A controller; RCM/RCM_TST -> PCS_X
finding: Phase-sensor and residual-current interfaces are not final qualified circuits. A power-board RFQ range is not a substitute for the controller's exact gain, output reference, linear overload range and fault behavior. The phase-sensor linearity requirement reaches beyond a simple +/-500 A label once the real trip band is used. RCM scale, trip timing, self-test and failure reaction need a specific sensor.
evidence: CODE-VERIFIED; REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY. Sources S12 S13 S14
recommendation: Freeze exact MPNs and datum-controlled interface limits. Recalculate all ADC/comparator bands and define RCM independent protection versus firmware responsibility.
closure: Phase-current sensor: the repository's earlier search missed that Sinomags' HO/2 and HO/4 families meet +/-500 A and >= 100 kHz (their catalogue summary line still says 125-375 A). Frozen to Sinomags STK-250HO/4 (I_PN 250 A, +/-625 A linear, 3.2 mV/A on an own 2.5 V reference pin, 200 kHz, 2 us max step, 4.3 kV rms / 8 kV impulse, > 8 mm creepage; datasheet docs/datasheets/sensing/Sinomags-STK-HO-4.pdf); PCS-PWR draws it, PCS-CTL's window ladders re-valued from its datasheet terms (gen/pcs_ctrl.py). Still open on that part: no working-voltage statement, no qualification statement, dv/dt immunity not stated (bench item, as the PV sensor). Residual-current sensor stays a request for quotation: no part found with 6 mA DC type-B detection AND >= 180 A per phase through three conductors; candidate class Magtron RCMU101SN-3P50G-6C (3 A range, 300 A through-current, 5 V, analog + reference pin, self-test); the applicable requirement is IEC 62109-2 style monitoring (300 mA continuous, 30/60/150 mA steps; standard text not on file), not the EV-charging 6 mA DC.

where: PCS-P125: L1=120 uH, L2=6 uH, Cf=50 uF -> current control, damping, PLL and grid-forming limiter
finding: Grid-following/forming stability and grid protection are not validated by the sizing study. The actual-board guide states control is not simulated. LCL resonance moves from about 9.42 kHz toward 2.05 kHz as grid inductance rises. Fundamental voltage feasibility and passive damping parts do not establish sampled-loop stability, THD, current-limited grid forming or anti-islanding.
evidence: CODE-VERIFIED; REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY; INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED. Sources S16 S17 S18
recommendation: Execute actual-plant GFL/GFM models with AFE/PWM delays, weak-grid and grid-fault cases, saturation and recovery. Implement a verified transfer and protection state machine.
closure: Control-validation gap closed by calculation (sim/pcs_control.py, sim/out/pcs_control/report.md; not measured): alpha-beta PR current loop on the converter current, crossover 1750 Hz stiff (K_p 1.39 ohm), resonant terms at h1/h5/h7; with the drawn R_d-C_d branch PM 67.9/56.0/56.4/48.7 deg and GM >= 12.1 dB at stiff/SCR 20/10/5 (rule PM >= 40 deg, GM >= 6 dB); without the branch the stiff grid is unstable (PM 1.4 deg) and active damping from the available measurements cannot replace it. 0.5 pu dip at 125 kW: 409-414 A peak inside the 422 A window edge; 0.1 pu dip 465 A trips (firmware item). SRF-PLL 30 Hz: PM 85 deg at SCR 5, loses the rule above 114 Hz. DC-link loop 40 Hz stable only with DC-current feed-forward (mandatory). Grid forming: terminal short limited at 366 A, no hardware trip; transfer and protection state machine with invariant checks; THDi estimate 1.5-2.2 % (assumed background). Not established: no switched model, no measured THD, no standards text, anti-islanding not simulated, four-wire not covered. Hardware findings: PCS-CTL ladder re-valued for the frozen sensor; the 'up to 1 kHz bandwidth' statement corrected; the DC link seen by a DC/DC is 0.41 mF (DAB study assumed 4 mF) -> power-ramp and trip coordination rule; full load at 600 V DC needs 672 V (stiff) / 790 V (SCR 5) when the grid is 10 % high (consistent with the PCM-05 envelope).

where: PCS four-wire: PWM7-16/VGN and IL4/IL4R unused in three-wire PCS_PC/PCS_X assembly
finding: The neutral power stage is not drawn in the reviewed assembly. Available PWM/ADC capacity does not supply a neutral leg, neutral inductor, sensor, contactor pole or its thermal capacity. Three-wire hardware cannot be sold as an equivalent four-wire unbalanced-load converter.
evidence: CODE-VERIFIED. Sources S12 S13 S16
recommendation: Create a four-wire assembly and compute neutral current, simultaneous device loading, modulation envelope, protection and transfer/bonding strategy.
closure: The three-wire assembly (PCS-PWR + PCS-CTL-3W rev A0) is documented as three-wire only: README, guide 09 and risk F9 state that the four-wire build is not drawn (fourth leg, neutral inductor, 4-pole disconnect, one more analog pin). No document claims the drawn boards cover a 100 % unbalanced load; AC-02 lists it for the four-wire version. Kept as a product derivative (risk F9); drawing it is a product decision, not a correction.

where: Repository: Model input loaders, generator specifications and derived reports
finding: Shared assumptions and fallback inputs can keep an obsolete model green. The reviewed loaders contain fallback/default pathways and share parameters with the implementation they check. Internal agreement does not detect a common unit, capacitance or current-definition error.
evidence: CODE-VERIFIED. Sources S02 S07 S17
recommendation: Fail closed on missing/stale dependencies; pin build hashes and units; add independent physical invariants and mutation tests which deliberately change a capacitor, gain, polarity or topology.
closure: Every reviewed loader now fails closed: sim/pv_control.py (the built-in trip/limit numbers when the spec is missing), sim/pcs_design.py, sim/port_design.py (the 96 kHz / 0.435 V ripple fallback), gen/pcs_power.py and gen/pcs_ctrl.py (magnetics insulation field, parsed sensor values, the sha256 stamp of the power-board check, the control-study plan), sim/dab_design.py and sim/dab_control.py (magnetics files, costed BOM, port spec, R_loop and P_branch_max defaults), gen/pv_power.py / gen/pv_ctrl.py / sim/pv_design.py / sim/pv_module.py, gen/cost.py (the silent board-list fallback). The earlier-platform CTRL-C2000 card now checks against a frozen snapshot of the control spec it was designed to (gen/data/control_spec_platform1.json) instead of the live cost-first spec. The shared-assumption point is answered by independent cross-checks rather than mutation tests: the inverter control study re-derives the plant from the magnetics files with its own three plant checks (worst error 0.13 %), the DAB fault chain was recomputed from the driver datasheet timing diagrams, the DC-link inventory is taken from the generator's own net list. Mutation tests and byte-for-byte reproducibility are not implemented (recommendation kept).

where: PV family: AUX75 SELV cross-regulation -> TPS54360B fan buck -> thermal airflow assumption
finding: Fan full-speed supply guarantees differ between power and control reports. The power-board reasoning uses a SELV supply of at least 24.5 V for full fans, while the control-board report states full-speed supply is guaranteed at S_24V >=25.6 V. This is not a proven fan failure, but the shared guarantee is not reconciled.
evidence: REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY; MECHANICAL-DEPENDENT; REQUIRES HARDWARE TEST. Sources S09 S10 S11
recommendation: Use one full-speed voltage/current/dropout contract, including buck duty limit and load loss, then update airflow and minimum live-load requirements.
closure: Two guarantees existed (PV-PWR: SELV >= 24.5 V at 100 % fans once the live rail carries >= 5.7 / 8.1 W; PV-CTL: full speed only at S_24V >= 25.6 V = set point + 1.5 V ASSUMED). One contract now: S_24V >= 24.50 V at the worst cross-regulation point, defined in gen/pv_power.py and read by gen/pv_ctrl.py, which derives the TPS54360B fan-buck output in dropout from its own drawn parts (D 0.99, R_DS(on) 0.24 ohm ESTIMATE, SS56, 203 mOhm choke) and asserts equality: PV-P75 23.59 V at 1.50 A -> airflow x0.983 (395 against 402 m3/h, R_sa x1.0059, sink 77.4 C, T_j 107.5 C), PV-P100/110 23.27 V at 2.21 A -> x1.000; inside the 3 % tolerance, so module_spec airflow is not derated (the build stops below 0.97). Assumed: fan speed proportional to voltage, airflow to speed, R_sa to Q^-0.34.

where: Family: Live controller / B1 barrier / custom T_BIAS4 and DAB transformer / PE and NTC interfaces
finding: Coating, altitude and custom barriers are not verified by the declared domains. The PV-CTL report relies on mandatory coating for a declared creepage shortfall at its assumed pollution degree and changes clearance above 2000 m. A domain checker, ceramic material conductivity or a transformer working-voltage label is not a qualified insulation system.
evidence: REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY; LAYOUT-DEPENDENT; MECHANICAL-DEPENDENT; REQUIRES HARDWARE TEST. Sources S03 S11 S20 S21
recommendation: Fix applicable standards/editions, voltage to earth, pollution degree, material group, altitude and coating process. Qualify spacing, barrier construction, partial discharge, dielectric tests and production process controls.
closure: Already registered as risk B1 (standards transcribed from memory) and the PV-CTL check's statement that the B1 barrier needs conformal coating for creepage at PD2 and more clearance above 2000 m. Nothing in schematic scope changes it: the applicable editions, pollution degree, material group, coating process and the custom transformer construction must be fixed with the standards text and tested; release gate, not a defect of the drawn boards.
